docs.text: OpenFilter ¶ Layered navigation for Magento 2 and Hyvä. Free and MIT, built on the OpenSearch Magento already ships. Multi-select filters with correct counts : options of a filter you use are counted as if it were not set, in one search request. AJAX that Varnish can cache : a filter click fetches the same URL a normal page load would, so the page cache serves it; CSP-clean on Hyvä, no reload, back button and scroll restored. Works without JavaScript : every option is a real link, sliders are forms. Sliders and built-in filters : price (display currency and tax aware) and decimal sliders, rating, in stock, on sale, new. Mobile drawer with "Show 123 products" counted before you apply. SEO rules : readable URL names, one canonical URL per page (301), robots and canonical tags, nofollow and a limit on combined values. Admin with diagnostics : Filters grid, a form per filter, "Why is this filter not showing?", openfilter:doctor . Start with Install . Questions and bugs: GitHub issues (triaged within 7 days, no SLA).

docs.text: Admin ¶ Everything lives under Catalog › OpenFilter : Filters (one list of attribute filters and built-in filters) and Settings (Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenFilter). Access is controlled by the ACL resources Catalog › OpenFilter › Filters and Stores › Settings › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenFilter . First run ¶ After installing, the admin shows a notice: how many filterable attributes OpenFilter found and which defaults it set (colours as swatches, sizes as text swatches, price as a slider, other lists as checkbox lists, Yes/No attributes as switches). Rating, In stock, On sale and New start switched off. Review defaults opens the Filters grid and dismisses the notice. Filters grid ¶ One row per filter: label, code, type (attribute or built-in), how it looks, several values, options before "Show more", search box threshold, "Google may index", position, storefront (shown or hidden). Inline edit : click a row, change the common fields, Save. Each row is saved on its own; a row with a value that does not fit (for example swatches on an attribute without swatches) reports its error and the other rows are still saved. Mass actions : Show on the storefront , Hide from the storefront , Reset to defaults (labels per store view and URL names are kept). Hiding a filter never changes the attribute's own "Use in Layered Navigation" setting, so it stays in the grid. Row actions: Edit and Why is it not showing? This changes published URLs; old URLs with option IDs keep working, old names do not. docs.text: Command line ¶ Command What it does bin/magento openfilter:doctor checks the installation and every filter, with the fix for each problem bin/magento openfilter:slugs:generate creates URL names for options that have none bin/magento openfilter:config:export writes filter settings, labels and URL names as JSON bin/magento openfilter:config:import <file> applies such a file, all or nothing openfilter:doctor ¶ bin/magento openfilter:doctor # default store view, every filter bin/magento openfilter:doctor -s de -c 21 # store view "de", also check category 21 bin/magento openfilter:doctor -f color --format=json It checks: OpenFilter enabled, no other layered navigation active, the search engine reachable with a product index, the count strategy in use, OpenFilter's cache enabled, every option with a URL name, and other modules that replace or wrap Magento's layered navigation classes (found in the DI configuration, reported by class name). Per filter it runs the checks of the admin's "Why is this filter not showing?" panel: shown on the storefront, used in layered navigation, field in the search index, and with -c whether the category has products with a value and more than one option. Each line is OK , WARN or FAIL . Warnings describe a choice or the catalog (a filter you hid, an attribute not used on search pages) and never fail. The command exits with 1 when a check fails, so it fits a deployment script. openfilter:slugs:generate ¶ bin/magento openfilter:slugs:generate --dry-run # what would change bin/magento openfilter:slugs:generate -a color # one attribute bin/magento openfilter:slugs:generate --overwrite # every name again from the labels Without --overwrite , existing URL names never change: published filter URLs keep working. Use it after importing options outside the admin (new options saved in the admin get a name on save). --overwrite regenerates every name from the current labels; old URLs then answer through the option-id fallback only if they used ids. openfilter:config:export / import ¶ See Import and export .

docs.text: Other search and filter modules ¶ OpenFilter works with the search engine Magento ships (OpenSearch, Elasticsearch 8 on 2.4.7). Two layered navigations on one page break each other, so OpenFilter steps aside when another one is active: Active module OpenFilter ElasticSuite ( Smile_ElasticsuiteCatalog ) storefront off, admin notice Adobe Live Search ( Magento_LiveSearchAdapter , Magento_LiveSearchProductListing ) storefront off, admin notice Stepping aside means: no OpenFilter plugins on the search request, no OpenFilter templates, no URL redirects; the other module's layered navigation works as before. The admin shows a notice naming the module. bin/magento openfilter:doctor reports it too, together with any other module that replaces or wraps Magento's layered navigation classes. OpenFilter does not replace Magento's search or relevance, and adds no index of its own: its fields live in Magento's product search index. An ElasticSuite adapter (OpenFilter's AJAX and SEO rules on top of ElasticSuite's filters) is planned for 1.2.

docs.text: Facet counts ¶ Multi-select filters need disjunctive counts : with "Red" selected, the colour filter must still show how many products are blue, green or black, while every other filter counts only red products. Magento computes every aggregation under every active filter (conjunctive counts), so a multi-select colour filter would show 0 next to every other colour. OpenFilter fixes this behind one interface, Iranimij\OpenFilter\Api\FacetCountStrategyInterface , with two strategies. Strategies ¶ Strategy Code Search requests How SingleQuery (preferred) single_query same as core Active facet filters move from the query to post_filter (they still narrow the products), and each aggregation is wrapped in a filter aggregation that holds every active facet filter except the ones on its own attribute. One round trip. PerAttribute (fallback) per_attribute core + 1 per attribute with an active filter The main request stays as Magento builds it. For each attribute with an active filter, one extra request (no hits, only that attribute's aggregation) runs without that attribute's own filter. Setting: Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenFilter › Search engine › How filter counts are computed ( openfilter/search/count_strategy ): Automatic (default), or a fixed strategy. Automatic uses SingleQuery on OpenSearch, Elasticsearch 8 and Elasticsearch 7, and PerAttribute for any other engine. Debug mode writes the choice to the log once per process. Which filters are "facet filters": term filters in the must part of the layered navigation requests ( catalog_view_container , quick_search_container ) whose attribute also has a term aggregation. The category drill-down ( category_ids ), visibility , price ranges and search text stay as Magento builds them. Other search requests (GraphQL, widgets) are not touched. Where it hooks in ¶ Verified on Magento 2.4.7-p10, 2.4.8-p5 and 2.4.9 (source of magento/module-elasticsearch 101.0.7-p5, 101.0.8 and 101.0.9, module-open-search 100.4.1–100.4.3, module-elasticsearch-8 101.0.x): Magento\OpenSearch\SearchAdapter\Mapper and Magento\Elasticsearch8\SearchAdapter\Mapper both delegate to Magento\Elasticsearch\ElasticAdapter\SearchAdapter\Mapper::buildQuery() , identical on all three versions. An after-plugin ( Plugin\Search\MapperPlugin ) collects the facet filters from the request, builds their clauses with Magento's own filter builder, and lets the strategy rewrite the query. Both adapters then call Magento\Elasticsearch\SearchAdapter\Aggregation\Builder::setQuery() and ::build($request, $rawResponse) , also identical on all three versions. Plugin\Search\AggregationBuilderPlugin hands build() the response with disjunctive counts (SingleQuery unwraps its filter aggregations; PerAttribute runs its count requests there), and hands setQuery() the original query, because core's price-interval data provider re-runs that query and must see exactly what core would have sent. Term filters with several values become a terms query in core already ( Filter\Builder\Term ), so addFieldToFilter('color', [49, 50]) is an OR within the attribute without further changes. Evidence (M0 spike) ¶ Test/Integration/Search/DisjunctiveCountsTest builds its own catalog (three filterable select attributes, 36 products in an anchor category, 4 outside it), then for each strategy and four selections (one value; two values of one attribute; two attributes; three attributes with multiple values) compares the counts of every attribute with brute force: one engine request per option, with OpenFilter switched off, counting products matching every active filter except the attribute's own plus that option. It also measures the requests each strategy adds over core on the engine itself ( _nodes/stats query_total ). Environment SingleQuery counts = brute force PerAttribute counts = brute force Requests added over core Run 2.4.9, PHP 8.3, OpenSearch 2.5 (local fixture) 4/4 selections, all attributes 4/4 SingleQuery 0 ; PerAttribute = active attributes (1, 1, 2, 3) local, 2026-10-13 2.4.9, PHP 8.3, OpenSearch 2.5 (local fixture), M1 catalog : simple + configurable products, 3 customer groups (Wholesale tier prices, price range), 2 store views (German view hides one product), category and search pages 4/4 scenarios, all 3 attributes; also equal to the catalog's own PHP model 4/4 — local, 2026-10-13 ( M1CountsTest ) 2.4.9 / 8.3, 8.4, OpenSearch 2.12 pending pending pending CI full matrix (after hours) 2.4.8-p5 / 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, OpenSearch 2.12 pending pending pending CI full matrix 2.4.7-p10 / 8.3, OpenSearch 2.12 pending pending pending CI full matrix 2.4.7-p10 / 8.2, Elasticsearch 8.17 pending pending pending CI full matrix Decision (preliminary, confirmed when the matrix is green): SingleQuery on every supported version and engine; PerAttribute stays as the automatic fallback for unknown engines and as a manual setting. If a matrix leg fails for SingleQuery only, that engine/version is mapped to PerAttribute in etc/di.xml ( autoByEngine ) and recorded here. Test note (M1): core's fulltext collection takes Api\Search\SearchCriteriaBuilder from ObjectManager::get() , one instance per process whose filters are never cleared, and the search indexer caches its attribute list per process. A storefront request builds one layer collection, so shops are not affected, but tests that build many collections or create attributes after an earlier reindex must reset those shared instances ( Test/Integration/Catalog/SearchIndexReset , and a fresh criteria builder per collection). The M0 brute-force test runs with that reset too. Sliders and the request budget (M1) ¶ Magento's price filter (and every decimal attribute filter) is a dynamic bucket: the main request already carries an extended_stats aggregation for it, but core's interval algorithm sends one or two more requests to build price ranges. OpenFilter's sliders need only min, max and count, so on layered requests Plugin\Search\DynamicBucketPlugin answers dynamic buckets from the main request's stats (bucket value stats ), and range filters on those fields are facet filters like any option filter: the price slider's bounds ignore the price range itself, but respect every other filter. Measured on the engine ( DisjunctiveCountsTest::testSearchRequestsPerPage , SlidersTest ): SingleQuery = 1 search request per category page (products, disjunctive counts, price and decimal bounds), PerAttribute = 1 + active attributes; core needs more for its price intervals alone. Bounds are converted to the display currency and tax display of the store view ( Model\Search\PriceBoundsConverter , default product tax class rate).

docs.text: Filters ¶ Settings ¶ Every filterable attribute and every built-in filter has settings ( Api\FilterConfigRepositoryInterface , Catalog › OpenFilter › Filters: see Admin ): display type, multi-select, options before "Show more", search box threshold, expanded, option order (position, name, count), hide a filter with one option, indexable for search engines, position, label per store view. On install OpenFilter stores sensible starting settings: colour-like (visual) swatches → swatch multi-select, text swatches → swatch multi-select, other selects → list multi-select, decimals → slider, Yes/No → toggle. Price and category are on; rating, in stock, on sale and new are off until switched on. Storefront requests read the settings and URL names from the OpenFilter cache type (Stores › Cache Management): no database query for them. Saving settings cleans that cache and marks the full page cache invalid. Behaviour ¶ Multi-select (OR within an attribute, AND across attributes) with disjunctive counts: options of an active filter are counted as if that filter were not set ( Facet counts ). Options without products are hidden (Magento's "Filterable (with results)"), unless selected. A filter with a single option is hidden unless something is selected. Sliders (price, decimal attributes): bounds come from the same search request, ignore the slider's own range, and follow the customer group's prices; price bounds are shown in the display currency and tax display (default product tax class). Built-in filters : rating ("N stars and up"), in stock (only when out-of-stock products are displayed), on sale (per customer group and website), new ("Set Product as New" window, evaluated at request time). See Index fields . Coexistence ¶ When ElasticSuite or Adobe Live Search provides the layered navigation, OpenFilter switches its storefront part off and the admin shows a notice: never two filter systems on one page. Budget ¶ A category page with any number of active filters costs one search request with the SingleQuery strategy (products, counts, slider bounds, built-in counts) and no extra MySQL queries compared with Magento (measured in Test/Integration/Performance/BudgetTest ).

docs.text: The product list template ( Magento_Catalog::product/list.phtml ) renders section#product-list[tabindex=-1] containing the top toolbar, the grid ( .products.wrapper ) and the bottom toolbar (pager and limiter). It is identical in 1.4.2 and 1.5.2. Empty result: with no products the template prints only .message.info.empty ("We can't find products matching the selection") and no #product-list . OpenFilter's #of-results region must therefore wrap the product list block from layout, not live inside the list template. Sorter, limiter and view mode are not links: initToolbar…() builds the URL and sets location.href on change / click ( toolbar.phtml ). The AJAX layer intercepts these in the capture phase on #of-results : it reads the new value from the control, builds the URL from the current URL and stops the event before Hyvä's handler runs. The pager uses plain links. Region wrappers planned for M3: #of-filters (the leftnav block), #of-state (the state block, moved out of the filter block so chips sit above the results) and #of-results (a container around the product list block). Each region is a layout container ( htmlTag="div" htmlId="of-…" ).

docs.text: Hyvä ships Alpine 3.14.3 ( Hyva_Theme::js/alpine3.min.js ). It also ships alpine3-csp.min.js for strict CSP setups. Alpine.initTree(el) exists in 3.x and is what the AJAX layer calls on swapped regions after replaceChildren , so components inside product cards (add to cart, wishlist, swatches) start again. OpenFilter's component is written for both builds: x-data="openFilter" registered through Alpine.data , no inline expressions, and one inline script followed by $hyvaCsp->registerInlineScript() .

docs.text: Hyvä caches each product card for an hour. The key ( Hyva\Theme\ViewModel\ProductListItem::getItemCacheKeyInfo ) is: product id, view mode, template type, template, store, currency, the hide-details flags, the category id (only when categories are in product URLs), the customer group, the image display area, the image attributes and the tax rates. It contains no filter state . A filtered URL reuses cached cards, which is correct because a card does not change with the filters. OpenLabel's labels are part of the card HTML, so they survive every AJAX swap without integration code.

docs.text: OpenFilter's Hyvä package applies everything above through its own layout handles ( openfilter_hyva_layer , openfilter_hyva_category , openfilter_hyva_search ), added by an observer on layout_load_before only on layered category and search pages of a Hyvä theme while OpenFilter is enabled. Switched off, the page keeps Hyvä's stock templates (the "off" side of the Lighthouse gate). Verified on 1.4.2 and 1.5.2 (the local store runs 1.5.2 as a second store view, CI as the default theme): catalog.leftnav / catalogsearch.leftnav get layer/view.phtml : a <dialog id="of-drawer" open> around #of-filters , open in place on desktop and without JavaScript, modal on phones. catalog(search).navigation.state gets layer/state.phtml and moves into content above #of-results (a container around category.products / search.result ). After a swap: Alpine.mutateDom → destroyTree → replaceChildren → inline scripts not yet run on the page → Alpine.initTree , then hyva.initFormKey() (Hyvä fills form keys only on page load). Hyvä 1.5.2 renders stock swatches as a.swatch-option (1.4.2: a.swatch-option-link-layered ) and its toolbar amount without .toolbar-number spans; OpenFilter's own templates replace both on layered pages. docs.text: Import and export ¶ Move filter settings, labels and URL names between installations (staging to production, one shop to the next) as JSON. bin/magento openfilter:config:export -o openfilter.json bin/magento openfilter:config:import openfilter.json --dry-run # lists every change, writes nothing bin/magento openfilter:config:import openfilter.json Format (schema 1) ¶ { "schema": 1, "filters": { "color": { "settings": {"display_mode": "swatch", "multiselect": true, "logic": "or", "visible_options": 6, "search_threshold": 12, "expanded": null, "sort_by": "position", "hide_single_option": true, "seo_indexable": true, "position_override": null, "active": true}, "labels": {"de": "Farbe"}, "url_name": {"admin": "color"}, "options": {"Red": {"admin": "red", "de": "rot"}} }, "rating": {"settings": {"active": true}} } } Filters are keyed by attribute code or built-in code ( price , rating , stock , sale , new , category ); an attribute named like a built-in is attribute:<code> . Store views are keyed by store code; admin means all store views. Options are keyed by their admin label. When an attribute has several options with the same label, they are numbered in option order: "Wool #1" , "Wool #2" . Every section and setting is optional: a file may contain only what it changes. All or nothing ¶ The import first checks the whole file: schema, known filters, store views and options, value types, URL name format. Then it writes every filter inside one database transaction through the same rules as the admin (display types that fit the attribute, URL names unique per attribute and store view). If any value is refused, nothing is written and the command lists the reason and exits with 1 . --dry-run runs the same checks and writes inside a transaction it always rolls back, so URL name collisions are found exactly as in a real import. OpenFilter's cache is cleaned afterwards; Magento may show "full page cache invalidated" as after any admin save.

docs.text: Index fields ¶ OpenFilter's built-in filters (rating, in stock, on sale, new) are filterable and countable in the search engine, so they need fields in the product search documents. M0 verified the core extension points on Magento 2.4.7, 2.4.8 and 2.4.9 ( Test/Integration/Index/IndexHooksTest , run on every matrix leg). Extension points ¶ Need Core hook Notes Add values to each product document virtual type additionalFieldsProviderForElasticsearch ( Magento\AdvancedSearch\Model\Adapter\DataMapper\AdditionalFieldsProvider ), argument fieldsProviders The argument of Magento\Elasticsearch\Model\Adapter\BatchDataMapper\ProductDataMapper , shared by the OpenSearch and Elasticsearch 8 engines. Core registers categories and prices here. A provider implements AdditionalFieldsProviderInterface::getFields(array $productIds, $storeId) and returns fields per product id, batched. Declare the field types in the index mapping virtual type elasticsearch5FieldProvider ( Magento\Elasticsearch\Model\Adapter\FieldMapper\Product\CompositeFieldProvider ), argument providers (core: static , dynamic ) Used by the OpenSearch and Elasticsearch 8 mappers. OpenFilter adds one provider for of_rating (integer), of_in_stock (integer), of_on_sale_<group>_<website> (integer), of_news_from / of_news_to (date). What reindexes a product's search document ¶ The catalogsearch_fulltext mview subscribes to the product entity tables ( catalog_product_entity , _int , _decimal , _datetime , _varchar , _text ), category and website assignments, links, and catalogrule_product_price . Consequences: Field Reindexed by core? M1 action of_on_sale_* Price, special price and dates (entity tables) and catalog price rules: yes . A special price whose date window opens or closes changes nothing in these tables. Plugin after the price indexer's row/full actions: reindex the same products in the search index (Magento refreshes the price index for date windows daily). of_news_from / of_news_to Yes (datetime table). Compared to "now" in the store timezone at query time, so no daily reindex is needed. none of_rating No : review_entity_summary is not subscribed. Plugin after review aggregation: reindex the product's search document. of_in_stock Not through the mview ( cataloginventory_stock_item is not subscribed). With MSI, Magento_InventoryCatalogSearch reindexes on salability changes ( UpdateFulltextIndexOnProductSalabilityChange ). Legacy stock: product save. Legacy stock: plugin after the stock indexer's row action. Built-in filters (M1) ¶ Filter Index field Source Applied and counted Rating "N stars and up" of_rating (0–100, store view) review_entity_summary of_rating ≥ N × 20 ; one range aggregation for 4, 3, 2 and 1 stars In stock of_in_stock (0/1) MSI stock of the website ( inventory_stock_<id> ), legacy cataloginventory_stock_status without MSI term; only when "Display out of stock products" is on (otherwise every listed product is in stock and the filter is hidden) On sale of_on_sale_<group>_<website> (1) price index: final price below the regular price term on the current customer group's field New of_news_from , of_news_to (dates, open ends filled) "Set Product as New" dates window compared to "now" in the store's timezone at query time The mapper adds each switched-on built-in as a clause (when selected) and a count aggregation, and registers it as a facet filter, so SingleQuery and PerAttribute exclude a built-in's own filter from its count like any option filter. Everything stays inside the one search request. Reindex triggers ( Plugin\Index ): review aggregation → product; partial price indexer runs (special price windows refreshed by cron) and legacy stock indexer runs → same products in catalogsearch_fulltext .

docs.text: SEO rules ¶ Filtered category pages multiply: ten colours and six sizes already make hundreds of URLs. OpenFilter keeps search engines on the pages worth indexing and out of the rest. The rules are conservative by default: only pages you mark can be indexed. Robots ¶ Page Robots No filter your store's setting (unchanged) Exactly one value of a filter with Let Google index pages filtered by this your store's setting (unchanged) Anything else: two values, two filters, a filter not marked, a category drill-down plus a filter NOINDEX,FOLLOW Search results with any filter NOINDEX,FOLLOW Mark a filter in Catalog › OpenFilter › Filters › (filter) › SEO . Good candidates are filters whose single values match what people search for: brand, colour, material. FOLLOW stays everywhere, so crawlers still reach your products. docs.text: Storefront (Hyvä) ¶ What shoppers get from iranimij/openfilter-hyva on Hyvä 1.4 and 1.5, how it behaves without JavaScript, and the markup contract themes can rely on from 1.0. What it looks like ¶ Filters in the sidebar, in the order of their position. The first three are open (setting Filters open by default ; per filter Open when the page loads ), the others are closed, and a filter with a selected value is always open. Each filter is a native disclosure ( <details> ), so it opens and closes without JavaScript and without moving the page. Options show their count. Options without products are hidden, except selected ones (so they can be removed). Lists longer than Options before "Show more" get a Show more (N) disclosure, and lists with more options than Search box from this many options get a search box that narrows the list as you type, including the options behind "Show more". Display types : lists with a check box, swatches (colour, image or text, always with a visible label and count), price and decimal sliders (two thumbs plus From / To fields), rating ("4 stars & up"), Yes/No switches (In stock, On sale, New and Yes/No attributes) and the category drill-down. Chips above the results: "Colour: Blue ×" removes one value, Clear all removes every filter and keeps the sort order. What happens on a click ¶ With Update results without reloading the page on ( Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenFilter , the default), a click fetches the same URL a normal click would load, so Varnish and the full page cache answer it. OpenFilter then swaps three regions: the filters, the chips and the results (toolbar, products, pager). The previous results stay visible under a thin progress bar until the new ones arrive. A cached URL takes about 70 ms on the test store. The browser history gets the new URL. Back and Forward restore the filters and the scroll position. The page title, robots , canonical and prev / next tags match what a crawler sees on that URL. The focus stays on the option you clicked. After removing a chip, applying the drawer or changing the page, it moves to the results. A screen reader hears the new product count ("22 products"). Sorting, products per page, the grid/list switch and the pager use the same swap. If the response is not a normal page (an error or a timeout), the browser simply loads the URL. If a range or a typed URL leaves no products, the chips show No products match. Remove the last filter with a link back. Phones ¶ Below 768 px the filters move into a drawer, opened by a sticky Filter (N) button above the results (N counts the active values). Changes in the drawer are staged : the drawer's filters and counts update, and the footer button reads Show 123 products . The page behind does not change yet. Show N products applies the staged filters without another request (the page was already fetched to count N). Close , Escape , a tap outside or the Back button discard the staged changes; the focus returns to the Filter button. Touch targets are at least 44 px, swatches at least 36 px. Without JavaScript ¶ Every filter is a real link ( <a href> ) to the filtered URL, so crawlers and shoppers without JavaScript filter by navigation. The slider is a GET form with From / To fields and an Apply button (steps: Price slider step for prices); the store answers with a 301 to the canonical URL ( price_from=20&price_to=50 becomes price=20-50 ). On phones the filters show as a plain list. The search box and the slider's thumbs are not shown without JavaScript. Search results ¶ The search results page has the same filters, chips, drawer and swap. Every link keeps the search query ( q ). Accessibility ¶ Filters are disclosures; options are links with "selected" announced for selected values ( aria-current ); colour is never the only signal (label, check mark, bold weight). Slider thumbs: arrow keys move one step, Page Up / Page Down ten steps; the number fields are the accessible fallback. The drawer is a modal dialog (focus kept inside, Escape closes it). Automated checks: axe-core finds no WCAG 2.1 A/AA violation in OpenFilter's markup on load, after a swap, in the open drawer and on a right-to-left store view. Right to left ¶ The stylesheet uses logical properties only, so a store view with <html dir="rtl"> mirrors the filters: counts on the left, chips from the right, the slider's lower end on the right, the drawer from the right. Content Security Policy ¶ The AJAX component is one static inline script, registered with Hyvä's CSP helper ( $hyvaCsp->registerInlineScript() ), and works with Hyvä's standard and CSP Alpine builds. Templates print no inline styles or handlers; swatch colours are SVG fills. After a swap, inline scripts of product cards run once per distinct script, so a store with a hash-only CSP allows them when the first page carried the same script. Markup contract (from 1.0) ¶ Themes can style or extend these; class names and attributes stay stable within 1.x. After every swap the window receives the event openfilter:swapped ( detail.url ); other components can listen to it. window.openFilter.navigate(url) swaps to a URL. Restyling ¶ view/base/web/css/openfilter.css (about 2.3 KB gzipped) uses only of-* classes and custom properties. ( view.phtml , group.phtml , state.phtml , filter/{list,swatch,slider,rating,toggle,category}.phtml , js/openfilter.phtml ). Keep the region ids and the data-of-* attributes when you do. docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ A filter does not show ¶ Run bin/magento openfilter:doctor -f <attribute code> -c <category id> , or open the filter in Catalog › OpenFilter › Filters and use Why is this filter not showing? . Both list each condition with its fix: the filter is shown, the attribute is used in layered navigation (category and search pages separately), its field is in the search index, the category is an anchor, products in it have a value, and there is more than one option. Counts look wrong ¶ Counts come from the search engine. After bulk changes outside the admin, run bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogsearch_fulltext . OpenFilter's counts are disjunctive: the options of a filter you already use are counted as if that filter were not set, so "Blue 12" next to a selected "Red" means 12 products if you add blue. Log and debug mode ¶ OpenFilter writes to var/log/openfilter.log . Switch on Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenFilter › General › Debug mode (it clears the full page cache) to get: log lines: the count strategy chosen for the search engine, why OpenFilter steps aside (another layered navigation), each request cut by the "most values" rule; attributes in the storefront markup, readable in the browser's inspector: Element Attributes #of-filters data-of-debug-strategy , data-of-debug-engine , data-of-debug-values (active values) each filter group data-of-debug-filter (filter key; "(core)" for Magento's own filters), data-of-debug-display each option link data-of-debug-option (option id or range), data-of-debug-count Keep debug mode off in production: the attributes are part of cached pages. Pages show old filters after a change ¶ Settings and URL names are cached in the openfilter cache type, cleaned on every save. The full page cache is marked invalid when a storefront setting changes; refresh it in System › Cache Management or with bin/magento cache:clean full_page . A theme changed the filter markup ¶ OpenFilter's templates can be overridden like any Hyvä template ( Iranimij_OpenFilterHyva/templates/... in your theme); keep the regions and data-of-* attributes listed in Storefront so AJAX updates keep working.

docs.text: Upgrade and uninstall ¶ Upgrade ¶ composer update iranimij/openfilter-hyva-bundle --with-dependencies bin/magento setup:upgrade OpenFilter follows semantic versioning: Api/ interfaces, the URL format, the storefront markup contract ( Storefront ) and the CLI JSON format change only in a major version. Magento's own layered navigation (and Hyvä's templates) return at once; settings and URL names stay. Uninstall ¶ For a Composer install: bin/magento module:uninstall Iranimij_OpenFilterHyva Iranimij_OpenFilter bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogsearch_fulltext This removes the packages, OpenFilter's six tables ( openfilter_* ), its settings ( openfilter/* ) and the record of its data patches, so a later install starts with fresh defaults. Keep the export of your settings first: bin/magento openfilter:config:export -o openfilter.json . The reindex removes OpenFilter's fields from the product search index. Magento's attributes and their "Use in Layered Navigation" flags are never changed by OpenFilter. iranimij/module-base stays installed while other iranimij modules use it.

docs.text: Filter URLs ¶ OpenFilter keeps Magento's routing and URL rewrites: filters are query parameters on the normal category or search URL, with readable, store-scoped names. /women/tops-women.html?color=blue,red&size=m&price=20-80&rating=4&stock=1 Filter Parameter Value Attribute (list, swatch) the attribute's URL name (default: its code) option URL names, comma-separated ( %2C works too) Price, decimal attributes price , the attribute's URL name min-max with . as decimal separator; open ends 20- and -80 ; price in the display currency Rating rating 4 = 4 stars and up (1–5) In stock, on sale, new stock , sale , new 1 Category Magento's own ( cat on search pages, the category URL on category pages) URL names ¶ Option URL names are generated once from the option labels: lower case, German transliteration first (Grün → gruen , Weiß → weiss ), any other script to ASCII, everything else becomes - . Collisions within one attribute and store view get -2 , -3 in option order. Store views get their own name only where it differs (German rot next to red ). Names never change because a label changed, so published URLs stay valid. New options get a name when the attribute is saved. Parameter names avoid Magento's own ( p , q , cat , product_list_* , ___store ) and the built-in filters ( price , rating , stock , sale , new ): Luma's sample attributes new and sale become new-2 and sale-2 . Old links keep working: a numeric option id is accepted in place of its name. Canonical URLs (301) ¶ Every filter URL has one canonical form: filters in position order, values in option order, URL names, lower case, no duplicates or unknown values. Category and search pages answer other forms with a 301 to the canonical URL; sort order, limit and view mode stay, the page number resets only when values were dropped. Other parameters (tracking, for example) may sit anywhere. POST requests are never redirected. Links OpenFilter renders are canonical already, so shoppers and crawlers never hit the redirect; it catches hand-written, old and external links and keeps one cache entry per filtered page. Reading and writing URLs in code ¶ Iranimij\OpenFilter\Api\UrlCodecInterface turns parameters into an Api\FilterStateInterface ( decode ) and back ( encode , urlFor ). Unknown parameters are ignored, values are checked against the attribute's options, numbers are clamped (price ≥ 0, ≤ 10⁹; rating 1–5).
